structure: Massachusetts History and Social Science Curriculum Framework (2018), part 2 of the file (u1195 onward): end of High School United States History I (Topic 7), then High School courses and electives each with an intro page (title, overview narrative with guiding questions, a boxed 'Standards for History and Social Science Practice, Pre-K-12' list that is split into several units, topic list, literacy note and 'connections' paragraph) followed by 'Content Standards' pages. Content standards are organized by Topic (codes such as [USII.T1], [WHI.T3], [GOV]/[T1]), each topic opens with a 'Supporting Question', then numbered standards 1..n with lettered sub-lists (a, b, c...), 'Clarification Statement' blocks, and 'Key/Suggested Primary Sources for Topic n in Appendix D' blocks; footnotes appear at page bottoms. Courses in range: United States History I (tail), United States History II, World History I, World History II, elective United States Government and Politics, elective Economics, Personal Financial Literacy, News/Media Literacy (HS stand-alone standard sets). Then Grades 9-10 and 11-12 Literacy Standards in the Content Areas (RCA-H, WCA, SLCA), Appendices A (English learners / students with disabilities), B (inquiry), C (using primary sources), and Appendix D (annotated primary source tables: column 1 source and annotation, last column the grade(s)/course(s) it is tied to; the World History table also has period header rows), ending with a note about the companion Resources document. All high school content is labeled grades 9-12 with the course name as written.
